titleEn: Fireworks provide a few minutes of joy, but the economic and environmental costs last much longer
titleZh: 烟花带来几分钟快乐，经济与环境代价却持续更久
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Every Bonfire Night, people pay for a box of fireworks so their friends and family can enjoy the colourful display. Within a few minutes, it’s all over. But the price on the box doesn’t reflect the hidden costs. The smoke inhaled by neighbours, the animals disturbed or the public services called out when things go wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 每年的篝火之夜，人们都会买一盒烟花，这样他们的朋友和家人就可以欣赏到五彩缤纷的烟花表演。几分钟之内，一切都结束了。但是盒子上的价格并没有反映出隐藏的成本。邻居吸入的烟雾，动物受到的干扰，或者当事情出错时，公共服务部门的呼叫。

paragraphs.en: It’s not a question about whether fireworks celebrations are enjoyable, but whether the people enjoying them are aware of – or actually paying for – their full cost. Economists call this a “negative externality”. A purchase benefits the buyer and seller, but some of its costs fall on people outside that transaction. Fireworks offer a particularly visible example because the enjoyment is concentrated in time while the consequences are spread among households, public services and wildlife. As a finance researcher, I think this concept is overlooked in the fireworks debate.
paragraphs.zh: 问题不在于烟花庆祝活动是否令人愉快，而在于享受烟花的人是否意识到--或者实际上支付了--烟花的全部成本。经济学家称之为“负外部性”。购买烟花对买卖双方都有利，但它的一些成本落在交易之外的人身上。烟花提供了一个特别明显的例子，因为享受集中在时间上，而后果则是在家庭、公共服务和野生动物中传播。作为一名金融研究人员，我认为这个概念在烟花辩论中被忽视了。

paragraphs.en: Consider injuries. Figures show that 123 hospital admissions in England attributed to fireworks in 2024–25. That is not a count of everyone injured: cases treated without hospital admission are excluded. Preventing such injuries may not cut the NHS budget, but it can free clinical time for other patients. In an overstretched health service, that is an economic benefit even if it never appears as a saving in the Treasury’s accounts.
paragraphs.zh: 以受伤为例。数据显示，2024- 2025年，英格兰有123人因烟花爆竹入院。这并不包括所有受伤的人：没有入院治疗的病例被排除在外。防止这种伤害可能不会削减NHS的预算，但它可以为其他患者腾出临床时间。在过度紧张的医疗服务中，这是一个经济效益，即使它从来没有出现在财政部的账户上。

paragraphs.en: Pollution creates another unpriced cost. The UK’s official air-quality monitoring has recorded short-lived spikes in fine particles around Bonfire Night, although bonfires also contribute and weather affects how quickly smoke disperses. The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs assigns a central estimated damage cost of £114,411 per tonne of fine particulate emissions (known as PM2.5), expressed in 2025 prices to account for inflation. This is not a figure for fireworks: calculating that would require information about their emissions and who is exposed. It does show why a product can have an environmental cost that never appears on its receipt.
paragraphs.zh: 污染造成了另一个无法计算的成本。英国官方的空气质量监测记录显示，在篝火之夜（Bonfire Night）前后，细颗粒物出现了短暂的峰值，尽管篝火也是原因之一，而且天气也会影响烟雾消散的速度。英国环境、食品和农村事务部（Department for Environment，Food and Rural Affairs）估计，每排放一吨细颗粒物，造成的损害成本为114,411英镑PM2.5，以2025年的价格来表示，以考虑通货膨胀。这不是烟花的数据：计算烟花需要有关其排放量和谁受到影响的信息。它确实表明了为什么一种产品的环境成本可能从未出现在其收据上。

paragraphs.en: Nature belongs on the balance sheet
paragraphs.zh: 大自然属于资产负债表

paragraphs.en: The damage is not limited to human health. In a peer-reviewed Dutch study, researchers found that approximately 1,000 times as many birds were flying during New Year’s Eve fireworks as on ordinary nights. The disruption extended several miles from the displays. The exact scale cannot be transferred to British Bonfire Nights, but the finding challenges the idea that fireworks affect only those who choose to watch.
paragraphs.zh: 这种损害不仅限于人类健康。在一项经过同行评议的荷兰研究中，研究人员发现，在除夕夜燃放烟花期间，飞行的鸟类数量大约是平时的1,000倍。干扰范围从燃放烟花的地方延伸了几英里。确切的规模无法转移到英国的篝火之夜，但这一发现挑战了烟花只影响那些选择观看烟花的人的想法。

paragraphs.en: Birds forced into sudden flight expend energy and lose opportunities to rest. Pets and livestock may also be distressed. Alongside noise and smoke, spent casings and other waste leave a physical footprint. Sustainability means considering these effects, not simply asking how much carbon a celebration emits.
paragraphs.zh: 被迫突然飞行的鸟类会消耗能量，失去休息的机会。宠物和牲畜也可能会感到痛苦。除了噪音和烟雾，用过的弹壳和其他废物会留下物理足迹。可持续性意味着考虑这些影响，而不仅仅是问庆祝活动排放多少碳。

paragraphs.en: Yet putting nature on an economic balance sheet requires care. The value of healthy ecosystems is real, but we should not invent a monetary figure for fireworks-related wildlife damage when credible national estimates are lacking. Some effects can be quantified; others must still inform decisions even without an exact price.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，将自然纳入经济平衡表需要谨慎。健康的生态系统的价值是真实的，但在缺乏可信的国家估计数据的情况下，我们不应该为与烟花有关的野生动物损害编造一个货币数字。有些影响可以量化;其他影响即使没有确切的价格，也必须为决策提供依据。

paragraphs.en: Fireworks also create value. They support retailers, display organisers and cultural celebrations, including Bonfire Night, Diwali and New Year. The UK government’s 2026 consultation reports that fireworks imports averaged £27 million a year from 2021 to 2024. That is the value of imports, not total industry sales and certainly not what Britain would save by banning them.
paragraphs.zh: 烟花还能创造价值。它们支持零售商、展览组织者和文化庆祝活动，包括篝火之夜、排灯节和新年。英国政府2026年咨询报告称，从2021年到2024年，烟花进口平均每年2700万英镑。这是进口价值，而不是行业总销售额，当然也不是英国禁止烟花所能节省的金额。

paragraphs.en: If households bought fewer fireworks, they might spend on a local community event, food or another kind of entertainment instead. They might equally save the money. There is no basis for promising that fewer fireworks would automatically increase jobs, GDP or tax receipts.
paragraphs.zh: 如果家庭少买烟花，他们可能会把钱花在当地社区的活动、食物或其他类型的娱乐上。他们可能同样会节省钱。没有理由承诺减少烟花会自动增加就业、GDP或税收。

paragraphs.en: But GDP and wellbeing are not the same thing. Treating avoidable injuries and clearing pollution may involve paid work without making society better off. The relevant comparison is between the enjoyment fireworks provide and the harm, resources and opportunities their use consumes.
paragraphs.zh: 但GDP和幸福感并不是一回事。治疗可避免的伤害和清除污染可能涉及有偿工作，而不会让社会变得更好。相关的比较是烟花爆竹提供的享受与使用烟花爆竹所消耗的伤害、资源和机会之间的比较。

paragraphs.en: The practical question is not simply whether to completely ban fireworks and take the joy out of Bonfire Night. It makes more sense to ask which forms of celebration produce the most enjoyment with the least harm. Organised displays, fewer private launches, predictable timings and wildlife-sensitive locations could change that balance. Drone and laser shows might offer alternatives, but they also require electricity and equipment; their sustainability should be assessed, not assumed.
paragraphs.zh: 实际的问题不只是是否要完全禁止烟花，剥夺篝火之夜的欢乐。更有意义的问题是，哪种庆祝形式能带来最大的享受，同时伤害最小。有组织的烟花表演、更少的私人发射、可预测的时间安排以及对野生动物敏感的地点，可能会改变这种平衡。无人机和激光表演可能提供替代方案，但它们也需要电力和设备;应评估而不是假设其可持续性。

paragraphs.en: This is especially timely. The government’s fireworks consultation closed in October 2026 after receiving more than 140,000 responses from members of the public, businesses, charities and other stakeholders.
paragraphs.zh: 政府的烟花咨询于2026年10月结束，收到了来自公众，企业，慈善机构和其他利益相关者的超过140，000份回复。

paragraphs.en: Policymakers now have an opportunity to assess the social costs alongside safety, business impacts and cultural value. A credible assessment would be honest about what the evidence shows, and about the nationwide economic savings that cannot yet be calculated. Because when a fireworks celebration leaves a bill for people who never attended, its market price only tells part of the story.
paragraphs.zh: 政策制定者现在有机会在评估安全、商业影响和文化价值的同时，评估社会成本。一个可信的评估应该是诚实的，既要了解证据显示的情况，也要了解目前还无法计算的全国范围内的经济节省。因为，如果一场烟花庆祝活动让从未参加过的人买单，那么它的市场价格只能说明一部分问题。
